等了那么久，还疯狂跳票，玩起来的质量实在是难评，甚至还会回档，直接给我半小时白打，操作界面也不如1代方便，角色还会掉贴图变成白人，爱情等级提升也不加属性，立绘动作也是抽象，美子的刺客弓弦是靠原力拉的，各种各样的问题一大堆，还有那联动奖励，还要买另外两个游戏才有，第一次见吃相这么恶心的单机黄油，而且一代移植过来的老角色，新CG也是一个没有，那你还移植过来干啥，越玩越上火，下次先玩完再支持 最后总结，拉了坨大的，不建议现在入手，我现在甚至不敢接着玩，害怕被回档 4.27bug: 美子爱情5级后显示解锁了新皮肤，但是啥也没有 2-N的图会出现桌子的小图标不知道啥情况 放角色的时候有概率不会显示攻击范围 那个荷叶成精会出现bug导致直接卡关，任何手段都攻击不到 技能动画本来就没有，不知道这个功能有啥用 bug修复也是，蓝图就加了个保存键，点了还是没有效果，保存不了 更新完又给我天赋整没了 做的食物需要退出再进入才会刷出来 爱情解锁画廊也是bug，我猫娘2级就解锁了 原皮的服装变化不影响小人，只有皮肤的小人会一起变 射箭的小游戏，不射完不会装填 点设置暂停有概率直接卡在设置界面不能继续游戏 正常游玩都是问题，这次就当买个教训了，bug比我用AI写的都多，还没买这个游戏的千万别买，等后面修完了再买，首发蠢灾难，之前的测试和跳票一点用都没有，现在的体验连半成品都不如，因为半成品只是内容不够，这个正式版我只感到敷衍，甚至每次更新都有不同程度的回档，真不如做成第一部的DLC卖，款我就不退了，别的作品我也不会再支持了。 4.28bug 时不时跳一个鹿娘出来好像是获得了什么，但是啥也没有，打怪也不掉落食材了 4.29bug 直接闪退了 5.4bug 从第三层开始无法正常获得新角色 无法烹饪 龙兰的CG没配音，没对话 龙兰的3阶会变成静止不动的裸体小人 技能动画巨糊 各种细小bug 意义不明无法触发的互动 漫画后面的对话跟梦话似的 5.5bug 龙兰的角色数值描述和实际不符 攻击范围有部分角色未翻译 神魔战场打不开，最后一个漫画解不开 鹿娘的胸罩脱了后外观会随机变化 弱智随从设计，切换角色麻烦的要死，角色的动态展示也是抽象的要死，感觉就像是几个人各做各的部分，没有交流沟通，最后用502粘一起 从各方面来说，除了小人的服装变化和战斗升级系统，别的包括优化，bug数量，CG质量，动态立绘都远远不如一代 5.16bug 神魔战场的对话框选项会叠一起
成就没反应，打完了4-5然后退出更新后把我存档更没了，想飞僵尸娘不得起飞💔

把主线都通关了，肉鸽模式也通关了一次（主要是这个模式bug太多了，经常出现中途卡住，重进后退回到第一次战斗的情况，连着玩了三局都中途卡住了，给我气笑了），简单评测一下 可玩性：本作延续了上一作的风格，都是类pvz游戏，但个人看来存在以下问题： 1、本作中战斗系统有所简化，局内升级不再区分攻击力、速度等分支，而是全都划为了能力，阵法系统也没了2、本作的数值平衡非常离谱，我在上一作偶尔还会卡关，这一作全程没有畅通无阻（尤其是在获得了丹鼎之后），不管是什么敌人什么机制，只要用美子+丹鼎就可以轻松过关，没有任何挑战难度，其他随从的存在感太低了 3、内容匮乏，无论是主线还是肉鸽模式，都和demo相差不大，如果你只想体验“游戏部分”，那只玩demo就够了，成品增加的内容非常之少，少到让人怀疑制作组在跳票的半年内到底有没有完善游戏 4、bug非常非常非常非常非常多，我玩了6个小时以及遇到几十个bug了，而且其中有不少都对游戏体验有较大的破坏，以制作组的产能（发售3天了他们甚至还没修好开屏看板娘变成白色虚影的bug），我不建议任何人在发售后的一个月内购买游戏 成人内容：共7个cg，每个cg基本上就是2张动图来回切配上剧情和配音（有一个没有剧情和配音，应该是还没做好），本作的新可进化随从都有一个额外场景可以互动，来自上一作的老角色各有一个新皮肤（和额外场景一样可以互动，并且可以在战斗中显示出来） 缺点：1、内容量明显对不起它的价格，不过后续活动一般会增加新皮肤或角色，如果制作组后面更新勤快的话也不是不行 2、明显不如上一作精细，上一作的立绘在不同裸露情况下的细节算是比较大的亮点，而本作在服装设计上就显得比较敷衍 优点：花样比较多，在纯爱向作品里算是相当放的开的了，而且可互动的部分很多，不只是单纯的播片 我至今仍认为妖谈1是我玩过的最好的黄油之一，所以在本作多次跳票（算上评论区和discord上说的大概有十几次吧，多到数不清了）后我仍旧选择在第一时间购买，但本作的体验实在糟糕，完全辜负了玩家的期望，我原以为demo是起点，没想到是巅峰。而且本作离第一个公告里说的完整内容还相差非常多，尤其是肉鸽模式（那个公告里说会有12个神对应不同方向的祝福，但本作实际上仍旧只有demo中已有的4个），和公告里说的完整内容作对比，本作连抢先体验都算不上，只能算是一个demo。如果一个制作组跳票多次后端上来一份还行甚至是一般的成品，我只会怀疑制作组的态度，但本作在跳票多次后的成品差到这种程度我都有点担心制作组是不是出什么变故了。总之，希望制作组后面更新和修bug勤快点，希望本作越来越好

It is very clearly rushed in its release state. UI is buggy, sound design is poor, and the translation is far from perfect. However, the core gameplay is solid just like the first game, and taking the first game's post-launch support into consideration I can quite confidently say that most of the present issues will be fixed in due time. Maybe wait a couple of months before purchasing if you want a polished experience.

[h1]Yaotan 2: Chronicles of the Nine-Tails[/h1] [b] [h3]Game Introduction[/h3] *Yaotan 2: Chronicles of the Nine-Tails* continues the story of the first game, with Hiro and his companions leaving Japan after the three-tailed fox senses a mysterious call from her true form, the legendary nine-tailed fox, somewhere in China. That sends the party into a new setting inspired by Chinese folklore while still keeping the yokai tone of the original. The story is not especially deep, but it does enough to give the campaign momentum. More importantly, the shift from Japanese mythology to a mix of Chinese legends and yokai helps the sequel feel fresh instead of just repeating the same formula with new skins. [h3]Gameplay[/h3] At its core, this is still a Plants vs. Zombies-style adult tower defense game, but it has more going on than a simple clone. Instead of only placing units and waiting, you also manage multiple resources, upgrade units during battle, use active skills, and move through a hex-map roguelite structure between encounters. That extra layer gives the game more variety than expected. Stage gimmicks are probably the biggest improvement over the first game. Different chapters introduce their own mechanics, such as special terrain, altered resource gain, rescue objectives, and unique boss patterns. Not every idea is equally polished, but the effort to keep the campaign varied is very noticeable. Unit progression is also satisfying. Yokai can evolve into stronger forms during a run, and that visual growth is part of the appeal. Outside the main stages, there is also a fair amount of progression through talents, quests, achievements, gifts, and side systems, which gives the game a stronger long-term loop. The main issue is balance. Some stages feel much better designed than others, and the launch bugs definitely hurt first impressions. A lot has already been fixed, but the game can still feel rough around the edges. Compared to the first title, it is also a little less immediately “fun” in the power-fantasy sense, because you cannot just flood the board as freely as before. [h3]R18 section[/h3] The adult side is handled well enough to justify the grind. The game has multiple heroines, animated uncensored scenes, skins, relationship-based unlocks, and a more detailed stripping/damage-state system than the first game. Even in battle, smaller visual details reflect those changes, which is a nice touch. The scene count is not huge yet, but the quality is solid. The art is attractive, the character designs are memorable, and the animated presentation is one of the better parts of the package. Skins also add a lot of visual variety, and the game feels fairly generous with character-side content overall. That said, this is still a gameplay-heavy title first. If you are only here for H-content, you may feel like the tower defense systems demand a lot before the payoff. Voice and presentation quality are also a bit inconsistent depending on the scene. [h3]Advantages and disadvantages analysis[/h3] 1.Advantages: ✔️ More gameplay variety than a basic PVZ-style clone. ✔️ Hex-map progression and extra systems add depth. ✔️ Unit evolution is satisfying both mechanically and visually. ✔️ Good character content, skins, and animated uncensored scenes. 2. Cons: ❌ Balance feels uneven in some later stages. ❌ Launch bugs damaged the first impression, and some roughness remains. ❌ Certain systems make the sequel less immediately than the first game. ❌ If you only want H-content, the gameplay may feel too demanding. [h3]summarize[/h3] Overall, *Yaotan 2: Chronicles of the Nine-Tails* is a sequel with real ambition. It adds more stage gimmicks, more progression systems, more side content, and a broader mythological setting, which makes it more interesting than a simple repeat of the first game. At the same time, that added ambition also makes it messier. Still, the strengths are clear: the tower defense core is solid, the evolution system is satisfying, the setting has personality, and the adult content is good enough to reward the effort. It is not flawless, but it is creative and content-rich enough to stand out in its niche. I haven’t played the first game, so I can’t really comment on the story connections, but this one has been pretty enjoyable so far. You could see it as a yokai-themed version of Plants vs. Zombies, or even a fun little yokai encyclopedia since I ended up discovering a lot of creatures I’d never seen before. There’s even a gacha-style system, which adds another layer to the progression and collecting.

Yokai Art 2: Tales of the Nine-Tails builds upon the strategic foundation established by its predecessor while expanding both its world and gameplay systems in meaningful ways. Developed by Secret Labo and published by Secret Labo, Reborn Entertainment, and Tora Creatives, the game blends tower defense, tactical strategy, and roguelite progression into an adventure inspired by Japanese folklore. The story follows Hiro after his victory over Fujin and Raijin, only for peace to be interrupted when Sanbi begins hearing a mysterious call tied to her forgotten origins as the legendary nine-tailed fox. This premise gives the campaign a stronger narrative drive, encouraging players to uncover ancient secrets while confronting supernatural enemies across a variety of mystical landscapes. At its core, the gameplay revolves around thoughtful planning instead of quick reflexes. Each battle takes place on grid-based maps where positioning allies correctly is just as important as selecting the right units for the encounter. Every stage introduces different enemy formations and combat challenges that reward careful preparation over reckless offense. Defeating hostile yokai grants spiritual energy that can be invested in strengthening the team, while Powerstones unlock evolved versions of characters with enhanced abilities and more devastating attacks. These progression systems create a satisfying loop of experimentation, allowing players to continually adjust their strategies while discovering increasingly powerful combinations capable of overcoming tougher battles and intimidating boss encounters. The roster of recruitable yokai is one of the game's biggest attractions. Every companion contributes unique strengths to the battlefield, encouraging players to build balanced teams instead of relying on a single dominant strategy. The roguelite elements also add replay value by making each run feel slightly different depending on the upgrades and character combinations available. Rather than becoming repetitive, the campaign steadily introduces fresh tactical considerations that motivate players to refine their approach as new enemies and abilities become available. Steam Cloud support and achievements further enhance the experience by providing convenient progression tracking and additional goals for dedicated players. Visually, Yokai Art 2 embraces a colorful anime-inspired aesthetic that fits its mythological setting remarkably well. Character illustrations are expressive, enemy designs are imaginative, and the environments effectively capture the mystical atmosphere of ancient legends. The combination of vibrant effects, supernatural creatures, and folklore-inspired architecture helps establish a memorable identity that separates the game from more generic fantasy strategy titles. The developers also openly acknowledge that certain visual assets, such as some icons and background elements, were initially generated with AI assistance before being refined by artists, resulting in an overall presentation that remains cohesive while allowing the team to focus on polishing the broader experience. Although the game delivers an enjoyable blend of strategy and progression, it is not entirely free from limitations. Players seeking fast-paced action may find the methodical pace of its tactical battles slower than expected, especially during later stages that demand careful resource management and precise positioning. The narrative serves its purpose by connecting the various encounters and giving Sanbi's personal journey emotional significance, but it remains secondary to the strategic gameplay rather than becoming the primary attraction. Likewise, while the optional mature character artwork may appeal to some audiences, it remains a relatively minor feature that never overshadows the game's focus on tactical combat. Overall, Yokai Art 2: Tales of the Nine-Tails successfully refines the ideas introduced in the first game while offering greater strategic depth, a stronger sense of progression, and an engaging mythological setting. Its combination of tactical combat, tower defense mechanics, collectible yokai, and roguelite systems creates a rewarding experience that consistently encourages experimentation and careful decision-making. Fans of strategy games inspired by East Asian folklore will find plenty to appreciate, while newcomers willing to invest time in mastering its mechanics will discover an adventure that offers satisfying challenges and steady progression from beginning to end. Rating: 8/10

[h2]简短介绍[/h2] 成人向植物大战僵尸+rouge养成的玩法、有爬塔模式。CG部分，动态步兵CG、日语全程配音，国区需要打补丁、外区有直接的DLC使用。CG主要触发方式是通过好感度，好感度达到就可以观看CG了，此外还有互动涩涩小游戏，需要抽奖或者多种方式解锁。 [h2]游戏内容[/h2] 这是第二部，虽然说是第二部，没有第一部的情况是可以正常游玩的剧情方面并没有硬性要求知道第一部的世界观，不过最好1+2)这样才有完整的体验 游戏新更新了九尾的时装，只需要在活动处完成一关即可兑换。大就是好，非常的涩气。 植物大战僵尸想必大家耳熟能详，就不用我过多介绍了。游戏需要花费灵魂(开局赠送以及击败敌人后获得)使用召唤妖怪来不让突破防线，游戏有几次机会，当被突破进入后院并不会结束，只是会影响游戏的关卡评级。 游戏有着完整的主线，并且有着不同的难度。每一关都会掉落元宝，元宝是游戏的货币，可以通过其抽奖、点亮卡牌的rouge属性、增加卡牌的能力。当然了，你说你不想点rouge能不能玩。能玩，到简单2-5左右就无法推过去了(别问我怎么知道的，我找打了六七次过不了开始找界面发现了rouge的存在)，数值还是存在的。 随着关卡，每一关都会有妖怪作为BOSS出场，击败后才可以进入一关，我们就能获得她们了。只是游戏的召唤并不非直接使用人外娘，而是从基础形态，如猫猫或者狐狸这种原型本体，进入游戏获得的灵魂对其增加到达4级就可以变成人外娘了。此外，人外娘会有皮肤，我们可以通过各种方式解锁这里不多赘述。我们作为主角也拥有自己的能力，可以让某一只人外娘变成完全体以及使用大招，又或者是召唤一些法术，为战局提供帮助(非常少的作用了，因为人外娘数值很强，不过用来保底也可以) [h2]最后[/h2] 爬塔、剧情部分还是挺有意思的，如果你想快速推关可以体验最简单的模式，想要挑战就爬塔以及推困难关(致敬传奇关卡最初的困难3-4之最无用的机关龟) 游戏目前的bug已经修复差不多了，可以完整游玩下来了。 [quote]关注「[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/45531088] 鸢尾花 [/url]」[/quote] [u][b] 致那一朵未至鸢尾花 [/b][/u]

《妖谈 2：九尾异闻》（Yokai Art 2: Tales of the Nine-Tails）是由Secret Labo制作并发行的一款类植物大战僵尸玩法的休闲塔防肉鸽小游戏。制作组之前还有个前作《妖谈：百鬼夜行》。 游戏的背景设定承接了前作的结局，主角紘战胜风神、雷神之后和可爱的老婆们在祖父家安稳的度过了一段日子。但有一天，三尾突然感应到了自己本体“九尾妖狐”跨越国界的神秘呼唤，为了追寻这个呼唤，主角紘与三尾和美子一行人在祖父的指引下前往东方国度，探寻九尾被封印、持续发出呼唤的秘密。 游戏的主要玩法还是和前作类似的“植物大战僵尸”类型的休闲塔防的框架，每个关卡都有几波的妖物抵御战，玩家需要在固定方格的棋盘赛道（院子），通过消耗妖之碎片（阳光）部署己方的妖怪单位（植物）来抵御敌方妖物（僵尸）的入侵。几个常见的单位，类似豌豆射手、卷心菜投手、坚果墙、冰炬树桩等定位的单位都有，使用起来简单易上手。主要区别就是游戏中的消耗品妖之碎片并非像向日葵产出阳光那样，而是开局自带一些，后续通过击杀怪物增加。妖之碎片除了部署己方单位，还可以用来强化单位的一些属性，像是攻击力、生命值等。除这些外，游戏还有着场外技能机制，可以让己方单位进化或者是直接攻击敌人。 涩涩方面，游戏本体不锁国区，但有一个R18的DLC锁区，可以通过打补丁的方式添加进游戏。本作中角色的立绘比起前作更加的精美，H事件数量偏少，动态CG、步兵无码、有做涩涩音效，后续好像还会再出一些DLC添加这方面的内容，整体质量还可以，给推荐。 [quote]关注「[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/45531088] 鸢尾花 [/url]」[/quote] [u][b] 致那一朵未至鸢尾花 [/b][/u]
